caption: Figure 1. General scheme for the proposed approach. The initialization step, the ﬁrst optimisation iteration without LLM proposal, and the main optimisation cycle are shown in blocks.
text_block: The following optimisation approach is proposed, with each element described in more detail in the following sections. Feature optimisation instance consists of a dataset, an LLM interface, and an LLM template. LLM template contains the information on the dataset, instructions, and possible options for the feature generation pipeline. If the initial advise option is enabled, the ﬁrst LLM query updates the template with the data insight to improve future proposals. On the initial iteration, a default feature generation pipeline is used to train the ML model, which type is deﬁned in the conﬁguration, and evaluate metrics to add to the template. The next iterations start from an LLM request for a pipeline, pipeline evaluation and a template update. The high-level scheme of the proposed approach is shown in Fig.1. the rest. Train and test data splits are created for each dataset, and each pipeline is ﬁrst applied to the train data, so scaling, PCA and other opera- tions do not result in data leaks between train and test datasets. Then the model can be trained, the type of which is deﬁned in the problem conﬁgura- tion. CatBoost [59], SVM Classiﬁer [61], and Random Forest Classiﬁer [60] classiﬁcation models are available for use; All the experiments shown use Random Forest Classiﬁer. Accuracy metrics and pipeline graphs are stored in the evaluation log and written to the LLM prompt. The new prompt is then used to obtain the pipeline proposal from the LLM, which is then parsed and used to initialise the new data operations pipeline. Another model training results are added to the log and prompt after evaluation, thus forming an optimisation cycle. The optimisation scheme is shown in Figure 1.
title: FEATURE ENGINEERING PIPELINE OPTIMISATION IN AUTOML WORKFLOW USING LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
visual_description:
1. The figure is a flow diagram titled "FEATURE OPTIMISER". A "Dataset Loader (OpenML)" on the left supplies a sequence of datasets, and a repeat symbol labeled "Repeat for each dataset" indicates that the complete optimization process is run separately for each dataset. The main optimizer is divided vertically into an upper configuration region, a base-template and initial-training region, and a lower iterative-refinement region.

2. The "Dataset Loader (OpenML)" contains entries "1", "2", "...", and "N", representing multiple datasets. A blue configuration connector runs between the optimizer's "Config" node and the loader, while a black connector sends the selected data into the upper "Dataset" node.

3. In the upper configuration region, "Config" controls four components through blue arrows: "LLM Interface", "Initial prompt template (Optional)", "LLM Template", and "Model". The optional initial prompt is directed to the "LLM Interface", with "advice" indicated beside this prompt-related connection. The upper "Dataset" also points into the "LLM Interface", and the interface produces or updates the "LLM Template". A dashed blue arrow carries the configured template into the next stage.

4. The middle region begins with an "LLM Template" containing a blue "Base Template" section. A solid blue downward arrow transforms this into another "LLM Template" labeled "0 Iteration Template", representing the initial generated template.

5. The middle-region "Dataset" feeds a "Default Data Transformation Pipeline". This pipeline specifies two operations: "Fill NaN with mean" and "Label encode categorical if possible".

6. The transformed dataset and the configured "Model" feed the process labeled "Initial model training". The resulting training output is directed to "Metrics + Graph".

7. The "0 Iteration Template" also points to "Metrics + Graph", associating the initial evaluation with the zero-iteration template. From "Metrics + Graph", a long blue arrow writes the evaluation output to "Results log".

8. A dashed blue connector passes from the "0 Iteration Template" into the lower refinement region, where an "LLM Template" contains the blue section "M-th Iteration Template". This is the current template at iteration M.

9. The "M-th Iteration Template" connects to an "LLM Interface". The lower-region "Dataset" and the interface feed a second "Default Data Transformation Pipeline", whose operations are "Parse transform operations" and "Validate on dataset copy".

10. The current template is refined into another "LLM Template" labeled "M+1-th Iteration Template". A dotted blue loop at the left, labeled "Iteration", links successive template states and indicates repeated refinement from one iteration to the next.

11. The validated transformation pipeline and the lower-region "Model" both feed "Model training". The trained model is then evaluated by "Metrics + Graph".

12. The lower "Metrics + Graph" node has two outgoing paths. One writes the iteration's evaluation to "Results log". The other provides feedback labeled "Add default pipeline If errors encountered", returning corrective information toward the next template so that a default transformation pipeline can be added when an attempted pipeline fails.

13. Overall, each dataset is configured with an LLM, an optional prompt, a template, and a model; a base data-transformation template is evaluated through initial model training; and subsequent LLM-generated templates are repeatedly parsed, validated, trained, evaluated, logged, and corrected when errors occur.
